title: Dedicated autoscaler: burst controls and utilization reporting improvements
author: Ethan Park
description:
Context: Customers running Redwood Dedicated reported tail latencies and unexpected throttling during short high-QPS bursts. The existing fleet autoscaler uses a smoothing window tuned for steady-state traffic which caused slower scale-up and opaque billing spikes. This PR introduces two complementary changes: 1) explicit burst controls that allow short-duration throughput overrides tied to a burst budget, and 2) richer utilization reporting so operators can see burst consumption and per-pool effective throughput.

What this PR does: - Add a burst budget primitive to the Dedicated Autoscaler config: burst_capacity (tokens), burst_rate (rps), and burst_window (seconds). When traffic exceeds the target throughput, autoscaler can consume burst_capacity to temporarily provision extra replicas faster than normal scaling rules. - Implement conservative burst drain and refill semantics so burst capacity recharges over time and is visible in metrics. - Expose new metrics: dedicated_pool_burst_used, dedicated_pool_burst_capacity, dedicated_pool_effective_throughput, and dedicated_pool_scale_actions. Metrics are tagged by pool_id and region. - Update the UI: Console now displays per-pool burst budget, recent burst usage timeline, and suggested burst configs based on historical traffic. - Add utilization reporting improvements: smoothing-window-aware utilization, p95/p99 utilization buckets, and hourly aggregated utilization export for billing reconciliations. - Tests: add unit tests for burst accounting, integration e2e test that simulates short high-QPS bursts, and new prometheus rules for alerts.

Migration notes: Default behavior is backward-compatible (burst_capacity=0). Clusters are unaffected until operators enable burst controls. Optional alerting rules are provided to detect burst exhaustion. Configuration schema bumped to v2.3; CLI upgrade script provided.

Why this matters: Enables predictable short-term throughput guarantees for Dedicated customers (e.g., seed traffic spikes, login storms) without permanent overprovisioning. The richer metrics make it easier to attribute cost and investigate incidents.

notes_for_ops: Default: burst disabled. To enable, set dedicated.autoscaler.burst_capacity and burst_rate in values.yaml and monitor dedicated_pool_burst_used. Alerts: fire when burst_used > 90% for 15m and p99 CPU > 85%. Use migration script cli/migrations/upgrade_config_v2_3.sh before rolling out.
